technique_remarks: order in which letters fell (end of the list from 35r): mim, dad, then the rest; compiler comments on the cipher author's design: the clear text avoids Allah (jalala, 'Allah' being quick to solve) and uses al-Rabb; changed the rhyme-letter (rawi) so as not to make it too easy; 'suhul al-hall' = ease of solution

contents.text: فحل ذلك سريعا وارسله مع كوني غربت فيه باشياء / منها اني جعلت في وله لفظة اي زائدة وانا للنداء وهي (?) / فقليلة الاستعمال بل نادرة الا في الموالليا ومنها / [ان لا؟] يكن فيه الف ولام متواليه فانها عون على الحل / ومنها جناس الالفاظ الاربعة في القافية ومنها ان[ت؟] / كتبت حلها بلا الف فيهما ولكن هذه موهبة من / الله تعالى وهو
contents.note: compiler's comments on the previous block (35v lines 8-13): 'fa-halla dhalika sari'an wa-arsalahu ma'a kawni ghurribtu fihi bi-ashya'' = I solved that quickly and sent it, though I had been misled (?) in it by things; 'minha anni ja'altu fi walah (?) lafzat ay za'ida wa-ana li-l-nida'' = among them that I put in it the word 'ay' as an extra (particle), and 'ana' for the vocative (?); 'fa-qalilat al-isti'mal bal nadira illa fi l-mawaliya' = so it is little used, indeed rare except in the mawaliya (verse form); 'wa-minha an la yakun fihi alif wa-lam mutawaliya fa-innaha 'awn 'ala l-hall' = and among them that there be no consecutive alif and lam in it, for they are an aid to the solution; 'wa-minha jinas al-alfaz al-arba'a fi l-qafiya' = and among them pun on the four words in the rhyme; 'katabtu halaha bi-la alif fihima wa-lakin hadhihi mawhiba min Allah ta'ala' = I wrote its solution without alif in both (verse lines) but this is a gift from God Most High; line 1-2 and the end of line 5 uncertain

contents.text: يا من لطراز ملك مصر حلا لمن مترجم اناه حلا / [?] لي لمر عيشي حلا ماحل [?] بازدكرن ملحلا
contents.note: verse in -ala rhyme answering the block 35v lines 8-13: 'ya man li-tiraz malik Misr hala...' = O you who ... the (embroidered) border of the king of Egypt became sweet (?) ... 'mutarjim' = ciphered/translator and 'hallaha' occur in line 8; line 9 mostly not read (tashrifak? li ... 'aysh? hala ma hall ...); the jinas of hala/hallan (sweet / solved / alighted) is the rhyme pun; words mostly uncertain

contents.text: ثم كتب الجواب ببيتين قديمين للعرب
contents.note: 'thumma kataba l-jawab bi-baytayn qadimayn li-l-'Arab' = then he wrote the answer in two old verses of the Arabs; introduces the next cipher (the cipher, then the 'old verses' as its plaintext)

technique_remarks: ten-ish design points the compiler lists for the verse: extra particle 'ay'; 'ana' vocative; rare mawaliya form; avoidance of consecutive alif-lam ('aun 'ala l-hall' - they help the solution); jinas of the four rhyme words; solution written without alif; 'mawhiba min Allah' = a gift of God (i.e. he solved it by inspiration)
plaintext_for: lines 1-9 relate to the block on 35v lines 8-13 (verse in lines 8-9); the block in lines 11-13 is answered by 'two old verses' presumably on 36v
certainty: low-medium: lines 1-7 readable in outline but several words doubtful; lines 8-9 low

contents.text: فلم ينحل الا بعد صعوبة عظيمة لغرابة الفاظه وقلة الف[ا]ظه / وكثرة واوانه خصوصا اخر الكلمة الاولى وهو نادر / الوقوع اخر الكلمات وتكراره في وجه وتكرر ميم / همت الى غير ذلك ومما
contents.note: 'fa-lam yanhall illa ba'da su'uba 'azima li-gharabat alfazihi wa-qillat ... wa-kathrat wawatihi khususan akhir al-kalima al-ula wa-huwa nadir al-wuqu' akhir al-kalimat wa-takraruhu fi wajh wa-takarrur mim hamtu ila ghayr dhalika' = it was not solved except after great difficulty, because of the strangeness of its words, the scarcity of (alif? / words), and the abundance of its waws, especially at the end of the first word, which is rare to occur at the end of words, and its repetition in 'wajh', and the repetition of mim in 'hamtu', and other things; first line end reading uncertain

contents.text: احوم عليك وفي فؤادي لوعة واصد عنك ووجه ودي مقبل / ومتى هممت بوصل غيرك دمتني وله اليك وشافع لك اول
contents.note: verse, waw-heavy as described in 7-10: 'ahum 'alayka wa-fi fu'adi law'a wa-asudd 'anka wa-wajh wuddi muqbil' = I hover about you and in my heart is passion, and I turn away from you while the face of my love is turned toward you; 'wa-mata hammamtu bi-wasl ghayrika ...' = and whenever I resolved on union with another than you ... first word of line 11 'ahum/ahuj' and line 12 middle words uncertain; 'wa-shafi' laka awwal' (and an intercessor for you first)

contents.text: فكتبتها وارسلتها الى بين يديه وكتبت حلها الجواب
contents.note: 'fa-katabtuha wa-arsaltuha ila bayna yadayhi wa-katabtu hallaha al-jawab' = so I wrote it and sent it into his presence, and I wrote its solution, the answer

technique_remarks: frequency observations on the cipher's plaintext: very many waws ('kathrat wawatihi'), especially at the end of the first word (rare word-final waw); repetition of 'wajh' (word) and of mim in 'hamtu'; strange words; 'inhall' after 'su'uba 'azima' = solved after great difficulty (compare 'fa-awwal ma inhalla' on 35r)
plaintext_for: cipher lines 1-6 here (with 36r lines 11-13) answered by the verse in lines 11-12
certainty: medium for lines 7-10 and 13, low-medium for lines 11-12; a catchword in the bottom-left corner (3 letters, not read)
